description: Ask the player to roll a move for their character: 2d6 plus the move's stat and skill. Give the target for a targeted move and the weapon it uses.

prompt.description: What the GM says to invite the roll. The player sees this text.

character.description: The name of the character who rolls.

modifier.description: A situational modifier from the story, not conditions; the engine adds conditions itself.

stat.description: The stat to roll, for a move the player chooses one for.

target.description: The character or threat the move is aimed at.

weapon.description: The weapon the move uses, when it uses one.

skill.description: The skill the move uses, for a move the player chooses one for.

practice.description: Whether this use marks practice. Defaults to true.

player_input.details: The engine adds the move's stat, the chosen skill, and conditions. Roll only the dice.

description: Apply harm to a character, NPC, or threat. Armor subtracts unless the harm pierces it; no turn or encounter is needed.

target.description: The character, NPC, or threat that takes the harm.

cause.description: What caused the harm, in the story.

piercing.description: True when the harm ignores armor. Defaults to false.

armor.description: Armor to use instead of the target's own, when the fiction calls for it.

description: Change a character's harm, infection, Rejection, Dread, or morale when the fiction moves it outside a move.

change.description: How much to add (positive) or remove (negative).

description: Start a named campaign clock, such as noise, horde pressure, a faction front, or a chase.

name.description: The clock's name; a content clock uses its id.

segments.description: How many segments the clock has. Defaults to 6.

visible.description: Whether the players can see it. Defaults to true.

description.description: What the clock tracks, when it is new.

description: Advance or set a campaign clock, firing its thresholds. Use it when the fiction moves a front, a chase, or the noise.

amount.description: How many segments to advance. Defaults to 1.

set_to.description: Set the clock to this value instead of advancing it.

description: End a campaign clock when what it tracked is over or no longer matters.
List the campaign clocks and their current segments.
Raise or lower the noise clock when the party is loud or quiet.

amount.description: How much to add (positive) or remove (negative). Defaults to 1.

reason.description: What made the noise, or what quieted it.

description: Create a threat at a location: a zombie, a horde, a horror, a survivor band, or an animal. Threats do not take turns.

name.description: A display name, such as 'the walker at the door'.

note.description: Anything the GM should remember about it.

description: List the active threats, their harm, armor, and location.
Show one threat's harm, armor, moves, tags, and location.
Apply harm to a threat. Its armor subtracts unless the harm pierces it.

piercing.description: True when the harm ignores armor. Defaults to false.

description: Record a threat's move, and apply its harm to a character when the move reaches one.

move.description: The move it makes, such as surge or bite.

target.description: The character the move reaches, if any.

harm.description: Harm to apply, overriding the threat's attack value.

cause.description: What the move looks like in the story.

description: Break a horde into individual zombies, lowering its magnitude or removing it.

count.description: How many zombies to create, from 1 to 12.

description: Merge a group of threats into a single horde.
Remove a threat that is destroyed, driven off, or gone from the story.
Create a party vehicle, such as a car, truck, or boat, with its fuel and condition.

name.description: A display name, such as 'the blue pickup'.

note.description: Anything the GM should remember about it.

description: List the party's vehicles, their fuel, condition, and location.
Damage a vehicle's condition from a crash, gunfire, or a hazard.

amount.description: How many points of condition to remove.

description: Add fuel to a vehicle, spending a fuel item the party holds.

amount.description: How many points of fuel to add. Defaults to 1.

description: Repair a vehicle's condition with parts and time.

amount.description: How many points of condition to restore. Defaults to 1.

description: Remove a vehicle that is destroyed, abandoned, or stolen.
Make an item from a recipe after the player's crafting check, spending the inputs.

character.description: The name of the character doing the work.

description: Strip a site or wreck for parts after the player's check, into a parts item.

character.description: The name of the character doing the work.

difficulty.description: The difficulty the check must meet. Defaults to 8.

amount.description: How many uses of parts to recover. Defaults to 1.

description: Restore one step of a carried item's condition after the player's repair check.

character.description: The name of the character doing the work.

difficulty.description: The difficulty the check must meet. Defaults to 8.

condition.description: The condition to set, when the fiction fixes it.

description: Swap one held item for another between two people, after the deal is struck.

giver.description: The name of the person giving an item.

receiver.description: The name of the person giving the other item.

give.description: The item the giver hands over.

receive.description: The item the receiver hands over.

description: Build a shelter improvement after the player's check, spending its cost.

site.description: The place where it is built.

character.description: The name of the character doing the work.

description: Damage a shelter's condition in an assault, fire, or storm.

amount.description: How many points of condition to remove. Defaults to 1.

description: Restore a shelter's condition with parts and work.

amount.description: How many points of condition to restore. Defaults to 1.

description: List the shelter's improvements, their progress, and their condition.

site.description: Limit the list to one shelter.

description: Record what an NPC wants next, so their off-screen moves stay consistent.

agenda.description: What they want and what they will do about it.

description: Add practice ticks to a skill outside a move, during downtime or teaching.

character.description: The name of the character learning.

ticks.description: How many ticks to add. Defaults to 1.

description: Teach a character a knowledge move they have earned through teaching, a manual, or experiment.

character.description: The name of the character learning.

feature.description: The knowledge move feature to learn.

description: Fill a firearm from a matching ammunition bundle the character carries.

character.description: The name of the character reloading.

description: Roll a generic dice table for weather, a road, a trade, the base, a rumour, a job, a threat, or an NPC. Do not use it for a typed site's room; search_site is the site's loot procedure and its zones, danger, and granular items are the point. The table id must be one this rule set defines, such as weather, road-event, trade-good, base-trouble, rumour, job, zombie-variant, horde-behavior, horror-sign, or name.

reason.description: Why the roll is being made.

patch.description: Move an NPC, a threat, or a character already in the scene; a player character crossing between settlement places uses navigate_city instead. Give the name and the destination; leave location out to send an NPC into the wind. Moving a player character to another place is a crossing, not a bookkeeping step, so use navigate_city and let the street, route, and City Alert matter. A place inside another takes the inner place's name.

description: Add a searchable site to the campaign from a site type. Read the kind with lookup_site_type and make this one unique with site-detail, site-secret, and your own detail before writing the description. A city site usually takes a parent, such as the street or block it sits on, and a small site inside a building takes the building's name. Give site_type so the party can search its zones with search_site. Set discovered only when the player already knows the place; a hidden or secret site must first be earned through a rumour, a map, a survivor, a sign, a radio call, or a named contact.

name.description: The place's name, unique among locations and NPCs.

description.description: What this place looks, sounds, and smells like, in a sentence or two, made unique by its own details.

site_type.description: The kind of site this place is.

parent.description: The street, block, or building this place is inside, if any. A place with a parent has no map point of its own.

discovered.description: True only when the player already knows the place.

summary.description: What the player sees in the compendium, with no GM-only secrets.

icon.description: An icon id from map_options' place_icons.

description: List the kinds of place this city can generate, filtered by find difficulty, category, or tier. Common sites are on any street; uncommon ones need a lead; hidden ones need a specific rumour, map, or contact; secret ones must be uncovered through play and are never placed where the party can simply find them. Use a mix when building a block: several houses, a convenience store or fast-food place, and one or two rarer sites worth a trip.

find.description: Only site types this hard to find.

category.description: Only site types of this category, such as home, shop, food, medical, tech, faith, occult, civic, or military.

tier.description: Only site types of this tier, from 1 for a house to 5 for a bunker or research site.

description: Read a site type's seed description, find hint, zones, loot profiles, and suggested threats before creating a place of that kind. The description is the ruleset's baseline, not the place: make each one unique with site-detail, site-secret, and your own telling detail. Its zones are the rooms a scavenging loop searches, and each zone's loot is a granular list, not a bundle.

Search one zone of a typed site after the player's Scavenge or Salvage roll. Use this instead of roll_loot or give_item for a typed site; it marks the zone searched, raises the site's danger, and gives the character the granular loot the roll earns. A 10+ finds two items, a 7-9 finds one, and a 6- finds none. At site danger 3, 5, and 6 the site answers with a complication; use it, a threat, or the streets. A zone has nothing left after it is searched, so choose a different room or leave. Pass take false only when the player is looking without picking anything up.

site.description: The name of the typed location being searched.

character.description: The character doing the searching. They must be at the site.

zone.description: The zone, room, or aisle to search, by id or name. Leave it out to search the next unsearched zone.

total.description: The Scavenge or Salvage total the player rolled. Defaults to 8 when no roll was made.

take.description: Whether the character carries what is found. Defaults to true; a full pack leaves items behind.

condition.description: The condition of everything found. Leave it out for the band's own condition, or pass worn when the player's 7-9 Scavenge cost was that the loot is in poor condition.

description: Move the party from one settlement place to another by a chosen route, raise City Alert by the route's cost, and roll a street event. This is the player character's movement tool between locations; do not use move_actor for that crossing. Use it for every crossing that matters: a main street is fast and watched, a side street is ordinary, and an alley, rooftop, building cut-through, or storm drain is quiet but has its own price. A street event is a beat, not a command; make it fit the fiction. When the party is carrying loot, wounded, moving at night, or City Alert is 3 or higher, call for a Navigate move before this tool.

character.description: The player character leading the crossing.

destination.description: The place the party is crossing to.

route.description: How the party crosses: main street raises City Alert 2, side street 1, and the other routes raise none but carry their own danger. Through buildings also makes noise.

reason.description: Why the party is crossing, such as hauling medicine home before dark.
